title: Prospective observational study of MRI-guided radiotherapy
summary: This is a targeted tumor treatment using MRI-guided radiation therapy. This novel radiation technique allows the treatment plan to be precisely adapted to the current position of the tumor and healthy organs at each session. This enables the tumor to be irradiated with the necessary dose while simultaneously sparing adjacent organs at risk as much as possible. Furthermore, it is possible to track tumor movement during irradiation in real time, thus ensuring highly targeted radiation. This innovative treatment concept is currently only available at a few centers worldwide, making precise documentation and quality control of MRI-guided radiotherapy essential. Within this study, the data routinely collected during radiotherapy will be recorded. No deviations from standard therapy are planned within the scope of the study. The target area and radiation dose are determined independently of study participation and comply with international and national guidelines, as well as internal clinical standards.
conditions: Various treatment regions treated with the MR-Linac are being investigated, including the central nervous system (CNS), head and neck, thorax, breast, abdomen/pelvis, and extremities.

interventions.name:
This prospective observational study aims to document and pseudonymously analyze the clinical outcomes of MRI-guided radiotherapy for quality control purposes.
Systematic assessment of the toxicity profile recorded in the clinic according to the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE
